problem: Given that ${\int }_{-2}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}$ and ${\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=2$ then what is ${\int }_{-2}^{1}(5+4f(x))\,\text{d}x?$

activity_context.topic_title: Properties of Definite Integrals Involving the Limits of Integration

feedback.worked_solution:
From the adjacent intervals rule, we know that

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{-1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Plugging in the known information gives

$$
(-6)+8={\int }_{-1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,⇒\,{\int }_{-1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x=2.
$$

Finally, compute the desired integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{5}(2f(x)+1)\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{-1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{-1}^{5}1\,\text{d}x \\  & =2(2)+x\,{|}_{-1}^{5} \\  & =4+(5-(-1)) \\  & =4+6 \\  & =10\end{aligned}
$$
